subject: estimates for multiple groups/species in mrds

messages.author: c3165650d54dd207
messages.subject: estimates for multiple groups/species in mrds
parts:
Esteemed colleagues,
I'm trying to fit a mrds model simultaneously to data from multiple species.  Data are sparse for some of the species, so I'd like to have some capability of sharing detection function parameters across species.  Looking through the help it doesn't seem like there's away to generate abundance estimates separately for each species using this approach.  Is this the case?  If so, maybe it would be worth adding this capability to the mrds "wish list" - e.g. allow a grouping variable in meta.data and use it to calculate separate estimates by group.

Cheers (and thanks!)
Paul

As a novice user, maybe I’m off-base, but I remembered this post from a couple years ago:

 

Hi listfolk, 

After an offlist discussion with Nathalie, I realised I misunderstood 
her question and that the answer I gave below is not correct. If one 
wants to obtain abundance estimates per *species* then one can use dht() 
from mrds. You can use the "subset=" option to dht to select a subset of 
the data to calculate the abundance estimates/densities. 

[NB To do the subsetting need the Region.Label and Sample.Label columns 
in the data, future versions of Distance for R will automatically do this.] 

Having fitted your model (called my_model, say) one can now calculate 
abundance estimates for a given species ("BW", say): 

dht(my_model, my_region.table, my_sample.table, subset=species=="BW") 

where the species column must exist in the data used to fit the model. 

Hope this helps. 


best, 
--dave

Just to clarify, I was able to use the dht() function in the mrds package to obtain species-specific estimates once I had fitted the detection model.  I simply used each species as a different "region"; region-specific estimates then corresponded to species-specific estimates of density and abundance.

Thanks again for the help.

Cheers, Paul
